title: The Tea Round
logline: Every night for years, a volunteer has pushed a tea trolley along hospital corridors for families who haven't left in days; on the night a patient finally goes home, the same trolley gets pushed a little faster.

object.note: Object 6 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From the day's rounds at the elders' home to night rounds in a hospital, where a volunteer's tea trolley reaches families who have not left in days.

thread_out.thread: Kindness meets the body's fragility: from the tea trolley's night corridors to a tea factory's night shift, where a watchman's body sinks with his sleep and has to be held up again.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Compassion for someone's worry and gladness at someone's good news are two different responses, and the texts say they take turns, each rising for the person actually in view. Someone who serves night after night is not in one fixed mood but meeting each person as they are.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: කෙනෙකුගේ කනස්සල්ලට දැනෙන අනුකම්පාවත් කෙනෙකුගේ සුබ පණිවිඩයට දැනෙන සතුටත් එකවර නොව, ඉදිරියේ සිටින පුද්ගලයා අනුව වාරයෙන් වාරය ඇති වන වෙනස් ප්‍රතිචාර දෙකක් බව අභිධර්මය කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The texts teach that compassion and sympathetic joy are occasional companions of a good mind: they arise only when a suffering or a happy being is the object. The Margaya says they are two different jobs and so cannot both be present in one mind at the same moment. The Pradeepika defines compassion by the wish to remove suffering and by not bearing others' pain, and its account of the sublime abidings moves from wishing someone's pain to end toward gladness at their good fortune.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Ordinary nights show the trolley on its round and quiet exchanges with relatives who have not left in days. On the night a patient finally goes home there are hugs and relief, and the same trolley gets pushed a little faster; that change of pace, not any narration, carries the shift from one response to the other.

key_terms.en: compassion (for the suffering) / sympathetic joy (for the happy)
occasional companion: a factor present only sometimes

lesson.caution: This does not mean a kind person is compassionate every moment; the texts describe compassion arising only when someone who is suffering is actually in view.
lesson.builds_on: The carers at the elders' home shifted between pain and good news within an hour; here the same shift runs across years of night rounds and one night of good news, as kindness meets the body's fragility.
